questions.question:
Simplify the following expression.

 2 (1)/(4) times 3 (1)/(5)+5 (1)/(6) of 2 (4)/(31) div 3 (2)/(3)+4 (1)/(7) of 1 (6)/(29) .
Ram and Shyam start walking from the same place in the opposite direction. If Shyam walks at a speed of 5(1)/(4)km/hr and Ram at a speed of 3 km/hr, then after how much time will they be 44 km apart?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two people move in **opposite directions**, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = 5.25 + 3 = 8.25 km/hr.

**Time** = **Distance** ÷ **Relative Speed** = 44 ÷ 8.25 = 16/3 hours.

16/3 hours = 5 hours + (1/3 × 60) minutes = 5 hours 20 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hr 20 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **Shyam** = 5¹/₄ km/hr = 21/4 km/hr

Speed of **Ram** = 3 km/hr

Total **Distance** apart = 44 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f173e594cd932837efe43a4fccc3d626aff764fd00ee0e9cd3d2ddb310236da9.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Relative Speed** (Opposite Direction) = Speed₁ + Speed₂

**Time** = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 21/4 + 3

⇒ **Relative Speed** = (21 + 12) / 4 = 33/4 km/hr

⇒ **Time** = 44 ÷ (33/4)

⇒ **Time** = (44 × 4) ÷ 33

⇒ **Time** = (4 × 4) ÷ 3 = 16/3 hours

⇒ **Time** = 5¹/₃ hours

⇒ **Time** = 5 hours + (1/3 × 60) minutes

⇒ **Time** = 5 hours 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hr 20 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their speeds: |S₁ − S₂|.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If a person covers a distance at speed x and returns the same distance at speed y, average speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: Rakesh is the owner of a rectangular field. Because of the construction of an expressway near his field, the length and breadth of his field are reduced by 30% and 10%, respectively. What is the percentage decrease in the area of his field?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Original length of the field = L

Original breadth of the field = B

New length of the field = 70% of L = 0.7L

New breadth of the field = 90% of B = 0.9B

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Decrease in Area = ((Original Area - New Area) / Original Area) × 100

**Calculation:**

Original Area = L × B

New Area = 0.7L × 0.9B

New Area = 0.63LB

Percentage Decrease in Area = ((L × B - 0.63LB) / L × B) × 100

⇒ Percentage Decrease in Area = ((LB - 0.63LB) / LB) × 100

⇒ Percentage Decrease in Area = (0.37LB / LB) × 100

⇒ Percentage Decrease in Area = 0.37 × 100

⇒ Percentage Decrease in Area = 37%

**The percentage decrease in the area of Rakesh's field is 37%.**

In which year was the percentage of rise / fall in production from the previous year the maximum for company C?

**2012:** 70 lakh

**2013:** 90 lakh

**2014:** 120 lakh

**Calculations:**

From 2013 to 2014:

questions.question: There are 160 multiple choice questions in a test. 4 marks are allotted for a correct answer and 1 mark is deducted for a wrong answer or un-attempted question from the total score of correct answers. If a candidate scored 400 marks in the test, how many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If all questions were answered correctly, the total score would be 160 × 4 = 640 marks.

The total marks lost from the maximum possible score = 640 − 400 = 240 marks.

Marks lost per incorrect or un-attempted question = 4 (for correct) + 1 (penalty) = 5 marks.

Number of incorrect or un-attempted questions = 240 ÷ 5 = 48.

Number of correctly answered questions = 160 − 48 = 112.

**∴ The correct answer is 112 questions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total questions = 160

Marks for a correct answer = +4

Marks for a wrong or un-attempted answer = −1

Total score obtained = 400 marks

**Method Used: Alligation**

⇒ If all 160 questions are correct, total score = 160 × 4 = +640

⇒ If all 160 questions are wrong or un-attempted, total score = 160 × (−1) = −160

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49a278fd89da73ac61af134bb9bb1e5ef4f35840483429dc4ad797f6ad27ef87.png] 

⇒ The ratio of Correct to Wrong questions = 560 : 240 = 7 : 3

⇒ Total ratio parts = 7 + 3 = 10 parts

⇒ 10 parts = 160 questions

⇒ 1 part = 160 ÷ 10 = 16 questions

⇒ Correct questions = 7 parts = 7 × 16 = 112 questions

**∴ The correct answer is 112 questions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation Approach

Let the number of correct answers be x. Then the incorrect or un-attempted answers will be (160 − x). The equation is formulated as 4x − 1(160 − x) = 400.

Rule of Alligation

It is a quick cross-multiplication visual method used to find the ratio in which two components of different values are combined to produce a specific average overall value.

Penalty Mark Evaluation

In negative marking exams, each mistake causes a total loss equal to the correct mark plus the penalty mark. For example, in this case, the total loss per error is 4 + 1 = 5 marks.
</p

questions.question: A seller decreased the selling price of each item from ₹5,000 to Rs. 4,680, by which his loss percentage increased by 4%. If he has to get 4% profit, then the selling price of the item should be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial selling price = ₹5,000

Decreased selling price = ₹4,680

Loss percentage increased by 4%

Desired profit percentage = 4%

**Formula Used:**

Loss% = (Cost Price - Selling Price) / Cost Price × 100

Selling Price for desired profit = Cost Price × (1 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price be CP.

Initial Loss% = (CP - 5000) / CP × 100

New Loss% = (CP - 4680) / CP × 100

New Loss% = Initial Loss% + 4%

⇒ (CP - 4680) / CP × 100 = (CP - 5000) / CP × 100 + 4

⇒ 100(CP - 4680) = 100(CP - 5000) + 4CP

⇒ 100CP - 468000 = 100CP - 500000 + 4CP

⇒ -468000 = -500000 + 4CP

⇒ 4CP = 32000

⇒ CP = 8000

To get 4% profit:

Selling Price = CP × (1 + 4/100)

⇒ Selling Price = 8000 × 1.04

⇒ Selling Price = 8320

**The selling price of the item should be ₹8,320 to get a 4% profit.**

questions.question: Two circles with centre O and A touch each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre O is 6 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre A is 3 cm. Find the length of their common tangent CB (in centimetres).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the first circle = 6 cm

Radius of the second circle = 3 cm

**Solution:**

**1. Distance Between the Centers:**

Distance between centers = 6 + 3 = 9 cm

**2. Length of the Common Tangent:**

Length of the common tangent = √[(6 + 3)² - (6 - 3)²]

Substitute the values:

Length of the common tangent = √[9² - 3²]

= √[81 - 9]

= √72

= 6√2

**Answer:**

The length of the common tangent is 6√2 cm.

questions.question: Two parallel chords of length 8 units each are 6 units away from each other in a circle. What is the radius of the circle in units?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two parallel chords, each of length 8 units, are 6 units apart in a circle.

**Formula used:**

For a chord of length 2a at a distance d from the center of a circle with radius r:

We use the formula for the distance from the center to the chord:

r² = d² + a²

Where a is half the length of the chord.

**Calculations:**

Let the distance from the center of the circle to one chord be d₁, and to the other chord be d₂.

Since the chords are 6 units apart, we assume one chord is 3 units above the center, and the other is 3 units below.

Half the length of each chord is a = 8/2 = 4 units.

For the first chord, the distance from the center is 3 units:

⇒ r² = 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 

⇒ r = √25 = 5 units

**∴ The radius of the circle is 5 units.**

questions.question: A cylindrical rod of iron whose height is twelve times its radius, is melted and cast into spherical balls, each of one-third the radius of the cylinder. Find the number of spherical balls.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Volume of Cylinder** to **Volume of Sphere** gives the number of balls.

Number of balls (n) = (π × r² × 12r) ÷ [4/3 × π × (r/3)³]

n = 12 ÷ (4 / (3 × 27)) = 12 ÷ (4 / 81)

n = 12 × 81 ÷ 4 = 3 × 81 = 243

**∴ The correct answer is 243.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** of the cylinder = r

**Height** of the cylinder (h) = 12r

**Radius** of each spherical ball (rₛ) = r/3

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of Cylinder** = πr²h

**Volume of Sphere** = 4/3 πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1178ea7f73775f5d1b7d89d6d5b6ddb0f140e247e12383a8e6448078f45d8556.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Volume** of iron = Volume of the **cylindrical rod**

⇒ Volume of cylinder = π × r² × 12r = 12πr³

⇒ Volume of one **spherical ball** = 4/3 × π × (r/3)³

⇒ Volume of one ball = 4/3 × π × (r³ / 27) = 4πr³ / 81

⇒ Let 'n' be the **number of spherical balls**

⇒ n × (4πr³ / 81) = 12πr³

⇒ n = (12πr³ × 81) / (4πr³)

⇒ n = 3 × 81

⇒ n = 243

**∴ The correct answer is 243.**

**__Additional Information__**

Conservation of Volume

When a 3D solid is **melted** and **recast** into another shape, the **total volume** remains constant, assuming no wastage.

Cylinder Surface Area

The **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of a cylinder is 2πrh, and the **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is 2πr(h + r).

Sphere Surface Area

The surface area of a **sphere** is given by the formula 4πr².

Volume Ratios

If dimensions are scaled by a factor k, the **volume** changes by a factor of k³.</p

questions.question: If the perimeters of two similar triangles are in the ratio of 4 ∶ 7, and the sum of the areas is 195 cm², then what is 1/3 of the difference between the areas (in cm²) of the two triangles?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Perimeter ratio of two similar triangles = 4 ∶ 7

Sum of the areas of two triangles = 195 cm²

**Formula Used:**

If the perimeters of two similar triangles are in the ratio a ∶ b, then their areas are in the ratio a² ∶ b².

**Calculation:**

Perimeter ratio = 4 ∶ 7

Area ratio = 4² ∶ 7² = 16 ∶ 49

Let the areas of the two triangles be 16x and 49x.

⇒ 16x + 49x = 195

⇒ 65x = 195

⇒ x = 195 / 65

⇒ x = 3

Area of the first triangle = 16x = 16 × 3 = 48 cm²

Area of the second triangle = 49x = 49 × 3 = 147 cm²

Difference between the areas = 147 - 48 = 99 cm²

(1/3) of the difference between the areas = 99 / 3 = 33 cm²

**The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Four cubes each of volume 216 cubic cm are joined end to end to form a new solid. The surface area of the new solid is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Side of each cube = √[3]{216} = 6 cm.

Area of one face = 6 × 6 = 36 sq cm.

Total faces in 4 cubes = 4 × 6 = 24 faces.

When 4 cubes are joined, 3 junctions are formed, hiding 3 × 2 = 6 faces.

Remaining visible faces = 24 − 6 = 18 faces.

Total surface area = 18 × 36 = 648 sq cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 648 sq cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of each cube = 216 cm³

Number of cubes = 4

**Formula:**

Side of cube (a) = (Volume)¹/³

Surface area of cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb2b8808275466f679d872530c2d660e264ffaf0409a13d8b3fedf2d43183f7b.png] 

⇒ Side of each cube (a) = √[3]{216} = 6 cm

⇒ When joined end-to-end, only the length changes.

⇒ Length (l) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

⇒ Breadth (b) = 6 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 6 cm

⇒ Surface Area = 2 × (24×6 + 6×6 + 6×24)

⇒ Surface Area = 2 × (144 + 36 + 144)

⇒ Surface Area = 2 × 324 = 648 sq cm

**∴ The correct answer is 648 sq cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a single cube with side 'a' is 6a².

Volume of a Cuboid

The amount of space occupied by a cuboid is given by Length × Breadth × Height (l × b × h).

Lateral Surface Area

For a cuboid, the area of the four side walls is 2h(l + b).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed in a cuboid has length √(l² + b² + h²).</p

questions.question: ∆ABC ∼ ∆EDF and area (∆ABC) : area (∆EDF) = 9 :4. If AB = 5 cm, BC = 8 cm and CA = 10 cm, then DF is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Areas** of similar triangles = Square of the ratio of **Corresponding Sides**.

Area(ΔABC) : Area(ΔEDF) = 9 : 4 ⇒ Ratio of sides = √9 : √4 = 3 : 2.

Since ΔABC ∼ ΔEDF, side **BC** corresponds to side **DF**.

3 units = BC = 8 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 8/3 cm.

2 units = DF = 2 × (8/3) = 16/3 = 5 1/3 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 1/3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ΔABC ∼ ΔEDF, AB = 5 cm, BC = 8 cm, AC = 10 cm, Area(ΔABC) : Area(ΔEDF) = 9 : 4.

**Formula:** If Δ1 ∼ Δ2, then Area(Δ1)/Area(Δ2) = (Side1/Side2)².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e32f5940a93af63ce7f9fc10d6d8ee7bfda40e3b1e9af986aee19292434e1bf3.png] 

For similar triangles ΔABC and ΔEDF, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

⇒ Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔEDF) = (BC / DF)²

⇒ 9 / 4 = (8 / DF)²

Taking square root on both sides:

⇒ √(9 / 4) = 8 / DF

⇒ 3 / 2 = 8 / DF

⇒ 3 × DF = 8 × 2

⇒ 3 × DF = 16

⇒ DF = 16 / 3

⇒ DF = 5 1/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 1/3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Side Ratio Theorem

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding sides, altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors.

Similarity Criteria

Triangles are similar if they satisfy **AA** (Angle-Angle), **SAS** (Side-Angle-Side), or **SSS** (Side-Side-Side) conditions.

Perimeter Ratio

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P1/P2 = s1/s2.</p

questions.question: If the area of a triangle whose base measures 6 cm is 18 cm2, then its height is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of the triangle = 18 cm²

Base of the triangle = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

**Calculation:**

Using the formula:

Area = 1/2 × Base × Height

⇒ 18 = 1/2 × 6 × Height

⇒ 18 = 3 × Height

⇒ Height = 18 / 3

⇒ Height = 6 cm

**The height of the triangle is 6 cm.**

questions.question: In an engineering college, there are four branches namely Computer Science (CS), Electronics (EC), Civil (CE), and Mechanical (ME). The respective ratio of the number of students in these branches is 11 ∶ 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 7. What is the percentage of students belonging to CS and ME branches in the college (correct up to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of students in CS, EC, CE, and ME branches = 11 ∶ 5 ∶ 6 ∶ 7

**Formula Used:**

Percentage of students in a branch = (Number of students in the branch / Total number of students) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the number of students in CS be 11x, in EC be 5x, in CE be 6x, and in ME be 7x.

Total number of students = 11x + 5x + 6x + 7x

Total number of students = 29x

Number of students in CS and ME = 11x + 7x = 18x

Percentage of students in CS and ME branches = (18x / 29x) × 100

⇒ Percentage of students in CS and ME branches = (18 / 29) × 100

⇒ Percentage of students in CS and ME branches = 0.6207 × 100

⇒ Percentage of students in CS and ME branches = 62.07%

**The percentage of students belonging to CS and ME branches in the college is 62.07%.**

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, one got 60% of the total valid votes and 15% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes were 8400, the number of valid votes that the other candidate got were:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Valid votes** = 100% − 15% = 85% of total votes.

**Other candidate's share** of valid votes = 100% − 60% = 40%.

Number of votes for **other candidate** = 8400 × 85% × 40%.

Calculation: 8400 × (85/100) × (40/100) = 84 × 85 × 0.4 = 2856.

**∴ The correct answer is 2856.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Total votes** = 8400, **Invalid votes** = 15%, **Winner's share** = 60% of valid votes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4801d45ed6f83b1b9b2ccf0fac4e57483117e19853a39cfbc020b10dd1b82b8.png] 

⇒ **Total votes** = 8400

⇒ **Valid votes** = 8400 × (100 − 15)/100 = 8400 × 85/100

⇒ **Valid votes** = 84 × 85 = 7140

⇒ **Other candidate's percentage** = 100% − 60% = 40%

⇒ **Votes for other candidate** = 7140 × (40/100) = 714 × 4

⇒ **Votes for other candidate** = 2856

**∴ The correct answer is 2856.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage of a Quantity

To find x% of a value y, use the formula: Value = (x/100) × y.

Valid and Invalid Votes

In election problems, **Total Votes = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes**. Candidate shares are usually calculated based on **Valid Votes** unless stated otherwise.

Successive Percentage Reduction

If a value is reduced by a% and then the remaining is distributed as b% and (100−b)%, the final part is: Total × [(100−a)/100] × [(100−b)/100].</p

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 8 years is 4/5 of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total interest in percentage = (4 ÷ 5) × 100 = 80%.

This **total interest** is for a duration of **8 years**.

**Annual Rate of Interest** = Total Interest % ÷ Time = 80% ÷ 8 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = 8 years

Simple Interest (SI) = 4/5 of Principal (P)

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bac66b9531ae05799380b395c1f777dff5341c3c2aa7694bb456d1ebd2e23410.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Principal (P)** be 5 units.

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = 4/5 × 5 = 4 units.

⇒ Using the formula: 4 = (5 × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 4 = (40 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 4 = 0.4 × R

⇒ R = 4 ÷ 0.4

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Components

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount throughout the entire **Time period** at a constant **Rate**.

Amount Formula

The total **Amount (A)** at the end of the term is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Rule of SI Variation

If the **Principal** and **Time** are constant, the **Simple Interest** is directly proportional to the **Rate of Interest**.</p

Find the total number of students selected for cricket and tennis.
questions.solution:
**Calculations:**

Total students = 1500

Cricket percentage = 35%

Tennis percentage = 20%

Students selected for cricket = 35% of 1500 = 0.35 × 1500 = 525

Students selected for tennis = 20% of 1500 = 0.20 × 1500 = 300

Total students selected for cricket and tennis = 525 + 300 = 825

questions.question: A class of 25 students took an English test. 15 students had an average score of 80. The other students had an average score of 60. What is the average score of the whole class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of students with an average score of 80 = 15

Average score of these 15 students = 80

Number of students with an average score of 60 = 25 - 15 = 10

Average score of these 10 students = 60

**Formula Used:**

Average score of the whole class = Total score of all students / Total number of students

**Calculation:**

Total score of 15 students = 15 × 80

⇒ Total score of 15 students = 1200

Total score of 10 students = 10 × 60

⇒ Total score of 10 students = 600

Total score of the whole class = 1200 + 600

⇒ Total score of the whole class = 1800

Total number of students = 25

Average score of the whole class = 1800 / 25

⇒ Average score of the whole class = 72

**The average score of the whole class is 72.**

questions.question: When x is added to each of the numbers 7, 11, 18 and 23, then the number so obtained are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between the (x - 1) and (2x - 10)?
questions.solution:
**Calculations:**

The numbers after adding x to 7, 11, 18, and 23 will be: 7 + x, 11 + x, 18 + x, and 23 + x.

Since they are in proportion:

7 + x / 11 + x = 18 + x / 23 + x

Cross multiplying, we get:

(7 + x)(23 + x) = (11 + x)(18 + x)

Expanding both sides:

161 + 30x + x² = 198 + 29x + x²

Canceling x² from both sides:

161 + 30x = 198 + 29x

Simplifying:

30x - 29x = 198 - 161

x = 37

Now, we need to find the mean proportional between x - 1 and 2x - 10.

x - 1 = 37 - 1 = 36

2x - 10 = 2(37) - 10 = 74 - 10 = 64

The mean proportional between 36 and 64 is:

√(36 × 64) = √(2304) = 48

**∴ The mean proportional between x - 1 and 2x - 10 is 48.**

questions.question: When the integer n is divided by 18, the quotient is x and the remainder is 6, When the integer n is divided by 25, the quotient is y and the remainder is 15. Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Express **n** in terms of both **quotients** and **remainders**.

n = 18x + 6 and n = 25y + 15.

Equating both: 18x + 6 = 25y + 15.

Rearranging: 18x − 25y = 15 − 6 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 18x − 25y = 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**n** divided by **18** gives **quotient x** and **remainder 6**.

**n** divided by **25** gives **quotient y** and **remainder 15**.

**Formula Used:**

**Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6820b9482e94e44ea90ff1e9bb3c37add58e65f6cbad7b9184c9d1fc8471a2fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: n = 18 × x + 6

⇒ Case 2: n = 25 × y + 15

⇒ Equating n: 18x + 6 = 25y + 15

⇒ 18x − 25y = 15 − 6

⇒ 18x − 25y = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 18x − 25y = 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Euclid's Division Lemma

For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

Linear Diophantine Equation

Equations of the form ax + by = c are solvable if the greatest common divisor (GCD) of a and b divides c.

Verification Rule

Always ensure the remainder is smaller than the divisor. If n = dq + r, then r must be in the range [0, d−1].</p

questions.question: Riya and Sangeeta can finish a work in 6 days and 8 days, respectively. Riya started the work alone and then after 3 days, Sangeeta joined Riya. They both finish the remaining work. How long did the total work last?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio of **Riya** and **Sangeeta** = 4 : 3 (Total work = 24).

**Riya** works alone for 3 days: 3 × 4 = 12 units done.

Remaining work (24 − 12 = 12 units) done by both: 12 ÷ (4 + 3) = 1 5/7 days.

Total time = 3 + 1 5/7 = 4 5/7 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 5/7 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Riya** = 6 days

Time taken by **Sangeeta** = 8 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **Riya**
 6
 24 (LCM)
 4
 
 

 **Sangeeta**
 8
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Work** = LCM of 6 and 8 = 24 units.

⇒ Work completed by **Riya** in first 3 days = Efficiency × Time = 4 × 3 = 12 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 24 − 12 = 12 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of **Riya** and **Sangeeta** = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day.

⇒ Time taken to finish remaining work = 12 ÷ 7 = 1 5/7 days.

⇒ Total duration of work = 3 days + 1 5/7 days = 4 5/7 days.

Therefore, the total time the work lasted is 4 5/7 days, which corresponds to **Option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 5/7 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a work. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Combined Work Formula

If A does work in 'x' days and B in 'y' days, together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days to complete the **entire** work.

Partial Work Remaining

When a person leaves or joins, always subtract the work already **done** from the **total work** to find the remaining task.</p
